quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: A pentagon-shaped sign warns you that a school zone is near or you are in one. Watch for children and obey the posted speed limits.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean that passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction of travel.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:

options.text: About three seconds have passed.
You can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
You can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, move back to the right lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe to take while driving if you take the recommended dose.
All medicines prescribed by a doctor are safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines, whether prescribed or over-the-counter, can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can cause drowsiness. Know how your medicine affects you before driving.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels not point straight ahead?

options.text: While waiting at a traffic light to turn left.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a light, keep wheels straight until it is safe to turn. If hit from behind, this prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic. On a hill, angle your wheels so the car rolls into the curb, not into traffic, if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control for better control.
Change your speed and direction slowly.
Drive the same way you normally do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction slowly.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make slow changes to speed and direction. Do not use cruise control because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect other drivers and pedestrians to give you the right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked cars to leave room for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked vehicles. A person may step out suddenly. A parked car driver may start moving without checking for you.

questions.question: Vehicles behind a school bus with red lights flashing must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students have left the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm out, you must stay stopped until the lights turn off, the arm is pulled in, and the bus moves.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is coming, you should:

options.text: Slow down and wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass.
Keep your speed steady. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you need to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is near, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
Only look in the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Check several times as needed. Keep watching traffic ahead and in the next lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: If your car loses grip on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at a steady speed to gain better grip.
Brake hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving fast in heavy rain, your tires can lose contact with the road and ride on water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not brake.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Looking straight ahead at the road.
Checking your mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware of hazards. Staring only at the road ahead is unsafe. In fog, use low beams instead of high beams.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles travel at about the same speed.
One lane is faster than other lanes.
One vehicle is faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Speeding increases crash risk. Going too slow also causes crashes because other cars may hit you from behind or swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: If someone passes you in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down so the other driver can safely get back in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver can safely get back in your lane.
questions.explanation: Let the passing vehicle return to your lane safely and easily. This helps avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge and slow down.
Move to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching the end of a divided highway.
You are approaching the start of a divided highway.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are approaching the start of a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is starting ahead. Stay to the right of the center divider.

questions.question: Motorcycles and scooters are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look constantly for them.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look constantly for them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot. You must always look carefully for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Sharp left and right turns ahead.
The road curves back and forth ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves back and forth ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road will curve back and forth. Slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down.

questions.question: You are merging onto an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Look for enough space to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there is no safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and collision severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and more severe crashes. Leave more space between cars as you drive faster.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing you.
Cars coming toward you.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: Let oncoming traffic pass before you turn left. Only turn when you can do so safely.

questions.question: The light turns yellow as you approach an intersection at the speed limit. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through without stopping.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Yellow means the light will turn red soon. Stop if you can do so safely. Otherwise, cross the intersection carefully.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than cars.
They brake more slowly than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you will not have time to stop if they brake suddenly.

questions.question: How should you pass on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Judge how fast oncoming cars are moving. Wait to pass until you are sure there is enough space. Oncoming cars often look slower than they are.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop (school buses, hazmat trucks).
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming. Watch for school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials, which must stop at all crossings.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Look at your rearview mirror often to see traffic behind you.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires you to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at high speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Interstate driving demands that you stay alert and can safely handle high-speed traffic.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to match the speed of traffic, then merge smoothly. Do not stop when entering an interstate.
